data.outcome_summary: This OECD framework proposes how PISA 2025 could measure “agency in the Anthropocene” among 15-year-olds, linking science education to knowledge, decision-making, hope, efficacy, and respect for diverse perspectives. The document defines three competencies: (1) explaining human interactions with Earth systems, (2) making informed decisions to act using evidence and systems/creative thinking, and (3) demonstrating hope and respect for diverse perspectives in seeking solutions. It outlines a draft cognitive proficiency scale (high/medium/basic/low) intended to be constructed from items aligned to Science Competency 1 and 2 with an environmental focus, while non-cognitive elements would be measured via an attitude questionnaire. It also provides example assessment item content and illustrates how the construct can be situated across socio-ecological crises and spatial scales (local to global). No empirical results, model performance metrics, or sampling/weighting procedures are reported because the document is not an analysis paper.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse because the provided text is an assessment framework and justification document, not an empirical study with an analytic dataset, model training, or reported performance outcomes. Consequently, there are no student-level results to tabulate, no PV estimation strategy to extract, and no missing-data or weighting procedures tied to an estimation pipeline. The document’s value is methodological: it specifies what should be measured in PISA 2025 and how cognitive and non-cognitive components could be operationalized through scales and item design.
